translationRepairs: On another day in the informal audience hall the emperor recognized his belt and questioned Zhi; terrified, Zhi told the whole story, and was removed to serve as military governor of Pingyi.
On another day in the informal audience hall the emperor recognized his belt and questioned Zhi; terrified, Zhi told the whole story, and was removed to serve as military governor of Tianping.
Chinese 罷為天平軍節度使 names the Tianping army (天平), not Pingyi; the proposed idiomatic corrects only that circuit name.

Another day, facing the emperor in the informal palace hall, the emperor recognized his belt and questioned Zhi; Zhi was terrified and explained the whole matter, and was therefore dismissed to serve as military governor of the Pingyi army.

Another day, facing the emperor in the informal palace hall, the emperor recognized his belt and questioned Zhi; Zhi was terrified and explained the whole matter, and was therefore dismissed to serve as military governor of the Tianping army.
The literal likewise has Pingyi for 天平軍; Tianping matches 天平, and the rest of the proposed literal matches the Chinese.
He was recalled to serve as military governor of Zhongwu and Xuanyi, and died.
He was recalled to serve as military governor of Zhongwu and Xuanwu, and died.
Chinese 忠武、宣武節度使 has 宣武 (Xuanwu), not Xuanyi; the proposed idiomatic restores the correct circuit name.
He was recalled to serve as military governor of Zhongwu and Xuanyi, then died.
He was recalled to serve as military governor of Zhongwu and Xuanwu, then died.
The literal also misreads 宣武 as Xuanyi; Xuanwu matches 武, and the proposed replacement corrects only that name.
In Shu there was Keyi County, directly southwest of Qiongzhou; the land was broad and level, with many springs suitable for irrigating glutinous rice.
In Shu there was Keyi County, directly southwest of Xizhou; the land was broad and level, with many springs suitable for irrigating glutinous rice.
Chinese 直巂州西南 names 巂州 (Xizhou), not Qiongzhou (邛州); the proposed idiomatic corrects only that prefecture name.
In Shu there was Keyi County, due southwest of Qiongzhou; the land was broad and level, with many springs, and could irrigate glutinous rice.
In Shu there was Keyi County, due southwest of Xizhou; the land was broad and level, with many springs, and could irrigate glutinous rice.
The literal likewise has Qiongzhou for 巂州; Xizhou is the correct reading, and the rest of the proposed literal is unchanged.
If we now divert southwestern garrison troops to farming, Yao and Qiong will be understrength and bandits can seize their chance.
If we now divert southwestern garrison troops to farming, Yao and Xi will be understrength and bandits can seize their chance.
Chinese 姚、巂兵少 pairs Yao with 巂 (Xi), not Qiong; the proposed idiomatic restores Xi and leaves the warning intact.
If we now divert southwestern garrison troops to farming, the armies of Yao and Qiong will be few and bandits can seize the opportunity.
If we now divert southwestern garrison troops to farming, the armies of Yao and Xi will be few and bandits can seize the opportunity.
The literal also misreads 巂 as Qiong; Xi matches 巂, and the proposed replacement corrects only that place name.
Shou himself wrote thanking the emperor, begging that his younger brother Yan die instead and continue their father's line.
Shou himself wrote thanking the emperor, begging that his younger brother Yan be spared so that he could continue the ancestral sacrifices of their late father.

Chinese 丐弟嚴死，奉先臣後 means begging that Yan be spared from death to continue the late father's line; context 乃宥嚴 confirms a plea for clemency, not that Yan die instead. The proposed idiomatic restores that sense.
Yang Shou, courtesy name Cangzhi, claimed descent from Yang Su, Duke of Yue of Sui, and said his family had long lived in Fupi.
Yang Shou, courtesy name Cangzhi, claimed descent from Yang Su, Duke of Yue of Sui, and said his family had long lived in Fengyi.
Chinese 世居馮翊 is Fengyi (馮翊), not Fupi; the proposed idiomatic corrects only that place name.
Yang Shou, courtesy name Cangzhi, claimed to be a descendant of Sui Duke of Yue Yang Su and that his family had long lived in Fupi.
Yang Shou, courtesy name Cangzhi, claimed to be a descendant of Sui Duke of Yue Yang Su and that his family had long lived in Fengyi.
The literal likewise has Fupi for 馮翊; Fengyi matches the Chinese, and the rest of the proposed literal is unchanged.
The next year he was exiled to Liuzhou; soon an edict recalled him for internal retention and ordered death by poison.
The next year he was exiled to Zhou; soon an edict sent an inner-court eunuch to pursue him and order his death by poison.

Chinese 流州 names exile to Zhou, not Liuzhou, and 內養追賜死 means an inner-court eunuch was sent in pursuit to grant death—not recall for internal retention. The proposed idiomatic restores both readings; poison follows the adjacent 仰鴆死.
The next year he was exiled to Liuzhou; soon an edict recalled him for internal retention and granted death by poison.
The next year he was exiled to Zhou; soon an edict sent an inner-court eunuch in pursuit and granted him death by poison.
The literal has the same Liuzhou and internal-retention misreadings of 流州 and 內養追; the proposed replacement correctly has exile to Zhou and an inner-court eunuch in pursuit granting death.
